why: I went through every PASS/FAIL pair in the verifier brief. Checks 1–3 cover behaviour lines, and each one runs the program on fixture files or stdin and records stdout, stderr and the exit code. None of them passes on reading the diff alone. None of the conditions is stricter than its line. Check 1 requires the files' output in argument order, matching the single-file runs. Check 2 requires a `-:1:` prefix and exit 2 for a second `-`. Check 3 requires exits 0/1/2/2 and an error on stderr, with files after the bad one still checked. The brief never fixes stderr wording; the advisory says "Stderr message wording is not fixed". It has no branch-name rule, no mutation test and no limit on which files the PR may touch. Check 4's no-diff condition applies only to src/index.js, which is what line 4 asks. The builder's "e.g." wording is guidance for the builder, not a PASS condition.
